I will keep my farm simple and stable this year. In Quzhou, I trust the wheat and summer maize system most because I know it fits our weather, our water conditions, and the way I can manage labor through the year. I will use improved or hybrid seed instead of old saved seed because I want more even emergence and better yield. For the winter crop, I will stay with winter wheat on all my land because it is reliable and easy for me to sell. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same land right away so I do not leave the soil idle. I will use rotary tillage for wheat after the previous crop residue is handled, and then lighter rotary tillage again before maize so I can plant fast. I will put enough nitrogen for grain production, but not too much, because too much makes the crop weak and wastes money. I will give phosphorus and potassium as base fertilizer to support roots and filling. I will irrigate wheat more times than maize because wheat here depends more on timely water in spring. I will spray only when needed, mainly to control weeds early and then pests or disease if pressure rises. My goal is steady yield, not chasing the highest possible yield with too much input.
